source_text: Τὸ μὲν οὖν ἄθεοι μὴ εἶναι, ἕνα τὸν ἀγένητον καὶ ἀΐδιον καὶ ἀόρατον καὶ ἀπαθῆ καὶ ἀκατάληπτον καὶ ἀχώρητον, νῷ μόνῳ καὶ λόγῳ καταλαμβανόμενον, φωτὶ καὶ κάλλει καὶ πνεύματι καὶ δυνάμει ἀνεκδιηγήτῳ περιεχόμενον, ὑφ᾿ οὗ γεγένηται τὸ πᾶν διὰ τοῦ αὐτοῦ λόγου καὶ διακεκόσμηται καὶ συγκρατεῖται, θεὸν ἄγοντες, ἱκανῶς μοι δέδεικται. Νοοῦμεν γὰρ καὶ υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ. Καὶ μή μοι γελοῖόν τις νομίσῃ τὸ υἱὸν εἶναι τῷ θεῷ. Οὐ γὰρ ὡς ποιηταὶ μυθοποιοῦσιν, οὐδὲν βελτίους τῶν ἀνθρώπων δεικνῦντες τοὺς θεούς, ἢ περὶ τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ πατρὸς ἢ περὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ πεφρονήκαμεν. Ἀλλ᾿ ἔστιν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ λόγος τοῦ πατρὸς ἐν ἰδέᾳ καὶ ἐνεργείᾳ· πρὸς αὐτοῦ γὰρ καὶ δι᾿ αὐτοῦ πάντα ἐγένετο, ἑνὸς ὄντος τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ. Ὄντος δὲ τοῦ υἱοῦ ἐν πατρὶ καὶ πατρὸς ἐν υἱῷ, ἑνότητι καὶ δυνάμει πνεύματος, νοῦς καὶ λόγος τοῦ πατρὸς ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ. Εἰ δὲ δι᾿ ὑπερβολὴν συνέσεως σκοπεῖν ὑμῖν ἔπεισιν, ὁ παῖς τί βούλεται, ἐρῶ διὰ βραχέων πρῶτον γέννημα εἶναι τῷ πατρί, οὐχ ὡς γενόμενον (ἐξ ἀρχῆς γὰρ ὁ θεός, νοῦς ἀΐδιος ὤν, εἶχεν αὐτὸς ἐν ἑαυτῷ τὸν λόγον, ἀϊδίως λογικὸς ὤν), ἀλλ᾿ ὡς τῶν ὑλικῶν ξυμπάντων, ἀποίου φύσεως καὶ γῆς ἀχρείας ὑποκειμένων δίκην, μεμιγμένων τῶν παχυμερεστέρων πρὸς τὰ κουφότερα ἐπ᾿ αὐτοῖς, ἰδέα καὶ ἐνέργεια εἶναι προελθών. Συνᾴδει δὲ τῷ λόγῳ καὶ τὸ προφητικὸν πνεῦμα· Κύριος γάρ, φησίν, ἔκτισέ με ἀρχὴν ὁδῶν αὐτοῦ εἰς ἔργα αὐτοῦ. Καίτοι καὶ αὐτὸ τὸ ἐνεργοῦν τοῖς ἐκφωνοῦσι προφητικῶς ἅγιον πνεῦμα ἀπόῤῥοιαν εἶναί φαμεν τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀποῤῥέον καὶ ἐπαναφερόμενον ὡς ἀκτῖνα ἡλίου.Τίς οὖν οὐκ ἂν ἀπορήσαι, λέγοντας θεὸν πατέρα καὶ υἱὸν θεὸν καὶ πνεῦμα ἅγιον, δεικνύντας αὐτῶν καὶ τὴν ἐν τῇ ἑνώσει δύναμιν καὶ τὴν ἐν τῇ τάξει διαίρεσιν, ἀκούσας ἀθέους καλουμένους; Καὶ οὐκ ἐπὶ τούτοις τὸ θεολογικὸν ἡμῶν ἵσταται μέρος· ἀλλὰ καὶ πλῆθος ἀγγέλων καὶ λειτουργῶν φαμεν, οὓς ὁ ποιητὴς καὶ δημιουργὸς κόσμου θεὸς διὰ τοῦ παρ᾿ αὐτοῦ λόγου διένειμε καὶ διέταξε περί τε τὰ στοιχεῖα εἶναι καὶ τοὺς οὐρανοὺς καὶ τὸν κόσμον καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ τὴν τούτων εὐταξίαν.
thought_title: Worship of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit
pass_a_gloss: The fact that we are not atheists, because we consider one ungenerated and eternal and invisible and impassible and incomprehensible and uncircumscribed, grasped by mind alone and word, encompassed by light and beauty and spirit and indescribable power, under whom all things have been made through his word and have been adorned and are held together, having been shown to me sufficiently. For we think also of the Son of God. And let no one think it laughable that the Son is of God. For not as poets mythologize, showing the gods to be no better than men, nor have we thought about God and Father or about the Son. But the Son of God is the word of the Father in idea and activity; for through him and on account of him all things were made, the Father and the Son being one. And the Son being in the Father and the Father in the Son, by unity and power of spirit, the Son of God is the mind and word of the Father. And if, because of excess of understanding, it seems to you to be examining what the child wants, I will say briefly that he is the firstborn of the Father, not as having been made (for God, being eternal mind, had the word in himself from the beginning, being eternally rational), but as the idea and activity proceeding before the material substances, of a divine nature and useless earth lying beneath, mixed with the thicker towards the thinner upon them. The prophetic spirit also agrees with the word; for it says, The Lord made me the beginning of his ways for his works. And we say that the Holy Spirit, which is at work in those who speak prophetically, is an effluence of God, flowing out and returning like a ray of the sun. Who then would not be at a loss, hearing us say God the Father and God the Son and Holy Spirit, showing both their power in unity and their distinction in order, being called atheists? And our theology does not stand on these things alone; but we also say a multitude of angels and ministers, whom the Creator and Maker of the world, God, distributed and ordered through his word, concerning the elements and the heavens and the world and the things in it and their good order.

bible_refs.note: The Lord made me the beginning of his ways for his works

pass_b_english: I have shown clearly enough that we are not atheists, since we worship one God who is ungenerated, eternal, invisible, impassible, incomprehensible, and uncircumscribed. He is grasped only by mind and reason, encompassed by light, beauty, spirit, and indescribable power. Under him all things have come into being through his Word, have been adorned, and are held together. We also acknowledge the Son of God. Let no one think it laughable that the Son belongs to God. We do not conceive of him as the poets mythologize, portraying gods no better than men. Nor have we thought about God the Father or about the Son in that way. Rather, the Son of God is the Word of the Father in idea and activity. Through him and because of him all things were made, the Father and the Son being one. With the Son in the Father and the Father in the Son, by the unity and power of the Spirit, the Son of God is the mind and Word of the Father. If, in an excess of scrutiny, you press to examine what the Child means, I will state briefly: he is the firstborn of the Father, not as having been made. God, being eternal mind, has possessed the Word within himself from the beginning, being eternally rational. Instead, the Word proceeded as idea and activity before the material substances, of a divine nature, with useless earth lying beneath, mixed with the thicker parts toward the thinner upon them. The prophetic Spirit agrees with the Word, for it says, "The Lord created me the beginning of his ways for his works" (Proverbs 8:22). And we affirm that the Holy Spirit, who works in those who speak prophetically, is an effluence of God, flowing out and returning like a ray of the sun. Who would not be perplexed to hear us call ourselves worshippers of God the Father, God the Son, and the Holy Spirit — showing both their power in unity and their distinction in order — and yet be labeled atheists? Our theology does not rest on these points alone. We also confess a multitude of angels and ministers, whom the Creator and Maker of the world, God, distributed and ordered through his Word to govern the elements, the heavens, the world, all that is in it, and their good order.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex theological distinctions of the Greek text, including the attributes of God, the relationship between Father and Son, and the nature of the Holy Spirit. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the Greek. The scripture citation (Proverbs 8:22) is correctly identified and added in Pass B as required.
